# llama-matrix

> llama-matrix measures how much memory each of your llama-swap models really uses, then generates a matrix block that lets as many models run at once as fit, without exceeding VRAM. macOS and Linux.

Measure how much memory each of your llama-swap models really uses, then let as many of them run at once as fit, without exceeding VRAM. The complete reference, for people and LLMs, is built into the tool: run `llama-matrix --llm`.
llama-matrix is one of the software projects by Jakob Hviid, all listed at https://jakob.hviid.phd/software/ (for LLMs: https://jakob.hviid.phd/llms.txt).

## What it does

- **Measures real footprints**: `measure` loads each model alone, waits for its allocation to settle and records the GPU memory it occupies, and host RAM the same way. A footprint is cached by its memory-affecting flags, so an unrelated config edit never forces a re-measure.
- **Declares everything that fits**: `build` finds every maximal combination whose measured footprints sum under the budget minus a safety margin, and checks each one against host RAM as well. `--budget` keeps room for other apps.
- **Applies, then checks**: `build --apply` backs up `config.yaml`, splices in the block, waits for the hot-reload and rolls back on any anomaly. `validate` loads the tightest declared combination and compares what it occupies with the prediction.
- **Made for scripts and agents**: Every command takes `--json`, and `llama-matrix --llm` prints the full guide, every command plus the design, for a person or an AI agent.

## Install

Homebrew, on macOS and Linux. Installs a prebuilt binary, so no compiler is needed. The tap is trusted once first, as Homebrew 6 and later ask.

```sh
brew trust --tap jakobhviid/tap
brew install jakobhviid/tap/llama-matrix
```

Or one line, without Homebrew. No compiler and no root: downloads the prebuilt binary to `~/.local/bin`.

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jakobhviid/llama-matrix/main/install.sh | sh
```

Or from source. Needs a Rust toolchain. The binary lands in `target/release/llama-matrix`.

```sh
cargo build --release
```

Then point it at your llama-swap, once. Finds your `config.yaml` and endpoint, detects the GPU budget and writes `llama-matrix.toml`. It needs a running llama-swap with the matrix engine.

```sh
llama-matrix setup
```
